title: Biological Waste Handling

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Proper segregation, containment, and decontamination of materials contaminated with biological agents before disposal.
explanation: Biological waste (contaminated pipette tips, culture plates, gloves, etc.) is typically segregated from general waste at the point of generation, placed in appropriately labeled biohazard containers/bags, and decontaminated (commonly by autoclaving) before final disposal, per institutional and applicable regulatory requirements.
keyPractices: Segregate biohazard waste into clearly labeled, appropriate containers at the point of generation.
Decontaminate (e.g. autoclave) waste according to institutional procedure before disposal.
Follow local/institutional regulations, which vary by jurisdiction and waste type.
commonMistakes: Mixing sharps into a general biohazard bag instead of a dedicated sharps container.
Assuming a biohazard bag alone (without decontamination) is sufficient for disposal.
